Both papers maximise "reward minus β times the log-ratio to the SFT model". They differ in three ways. InstructGPT adds a pretraining term to that objective. It fits an explicit reward model and runs PPO against it. DPO solves the plain objective in closed form and turns it into a single supervised loss on preference pairs.

## InstructGPT (Ouyang et al., 2022)

**Reward model.** It is trained on labeler rankings with a pairwise logistic loss, Eq. 1 ([p. 8](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/Training%20language%20models%20to%20follow%20instructions%20with%20human%20feedback.pdf?page=8&search=Specifically%2C%20the%20loss%20function%20for%20the%20reward%20model)):

$$\text{loss}(\theta) = -\tfrac{1}{\binom{K}{2}}\,\mathbb{E}_{(x,y_w,y_l)\sim D}\big[\log\sigma\big(r_\theta(x,y_w)-r_\theta(x,y_l)\big)\big]$$

**RL objective.** Eq. 2 ([p. 9](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/Training%20language%20models%20to%20follow%20instructions%20with%20human%20feedback.pdf?page=9&search=We%20maximize%20the%20following%20combined%20objective)):

$$\text{objective}(\phi) = \mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim D_{\pi_\phi^{RL}}}\Big[r_\theta(x,y) - \beta\log\frac{\pi_\phi^{RL}(y\mid x)}{\pi^{SFT}(y\mid x)}\Big] + \gamma\,\mathbb{E}_{x\sim D_{\text{pretrain}}}\big[\log\pi_\phi^{RL}(x)\big]$$

- **First term:** a fixed, learned 6B reward minus a KL penalty to the SFT model, applied per token. The paper says the penalty is there "to mitigate over-optimization of the reward model" (p. 9).
- **Second term:** the log-likelihood of pretraining data, weighted by γ. This is "PPO-ptx". Plain "PPO" sets γ = 0, and "InstructGPT" means the PPO-ptx model (p. 9).
- **How it is optimised:** PPO in a bandit setting (one prompt, one response, one reward), with the value function initialised from the reward model (p. 9).

## DPO (Rafailov et al., 2023)

**Objective.** DPO starts from the standard RLHF objective, Eq. 3 ([p. 3](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/Direct%20Preference%20Optimization.%20Your%20Language%20Model%20is%20Secretly%20a%20Reward%20Model.pdf?dest=section.3&page=3)):

$$\max_{\pi_\theta}\ \mathbb{E}_{x\sim D,\,y\sim\pi_\theta}\big[r_\phi(x,y)\big] - \beta\,\mathbb{D}_{KL}\big[\pi_\theta(y\mid x)\,\|\,\pi_{ref}(y\mid x)\big]$$

Here $\pi_{ref}$ is the SFT model. The paper notes that the usual practice is to fold the penalty into the reward, $r_\phi - \beta(\log\pi_\theta - \log\pi_{ref})$, and maximise it with PPO (p. 3). That is the first term of InstructGPT's Eq. 2.

**Derivation** ([p. 4](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/Direct%20Preference%20Optimization.%20Your%20Language%20Model%20is%20Secretly%20a%20Reward%20Model.pdf?dest=section.4&page=4)):
1. The optimum is known in closed form: $\pi_r \propto \pi_{ref}\exp(r/\beta)$ (Eq. 4; full derivation in App. A.1, p. 15).
2. Inverting it gives $r = \beta\log\frac{\pi_r}{\pi_{ref}} + \beta\log Z(x)$ (Eq. 5).
3. Substitute this into the Bradley–Terry preference model. Bradley–Terry depends only on reward differences, so $Z(x)$ cancels (Eq. 6).
4. The result is a loss on the policy itself (Eq. 7):

$$\mathcal{L}_{DPO} = -\mathbb{E}_{(x,y_w,y_l)\sim D}\Big[\log\sigma\Big(\beta\log\frac{\pi_\theta(y_w\mid x)}{\pi_{ref}(y_w\mid x)} - \beta\log\frac{\pi_\theta(y_l\mid x)}{\pi_{ref}(y_l\mid x)}\Big)\Big]$$

## How they differ

| | InstructGPT | DPO |
|---|---|---|
| Objective | KL-regularised reward **plus** the γ pretraining term (p. 9) | The plain KL-regularised objective, Eq. 3 (p. 3) |
| Reward | Explicit model $r_\theta$, fit first (Eq. 1, p. 8), shifted so labeler demonstrations score 0 on average (p. 8) | Implicit: $\hat r_\theta = \beta\log\frac{\pi_\theta}{\pi_{ref}}$ (p. 4) |
| How solved | PPO with a value network (p. 9) | Closed-form optimum, then a binary-classification loss; no RL loop (p. 4) |
| Data during training | On-policy: samples from $\pi^{RL}$ on about 31k API prompts (pp. 6, 9) | Offline: a fixed set of pairs sampled from $\pi_{ref}$ (p. 4) |
| Preference format | Rankings of K = 4–9 responses; all $\binom{K}{2}$ pairs from one prompt form one batch element (p. 8) | Pairs under Bradley–Terry (p. 3); rankings via Plackett–Luce in App. A.3 (p. 16) |

**What this means in practice:**

- **The pretraining term is outside DPO's derivation.** The closed form in Eq. 4 solves Eq. 3, which has no γ term. So DPO's equivalence result covers InstructGPT's plain "PPO" models (γ = 0), not the PPO-ptx model it shipped. InstructGPT added the term because RLHF lowered scores on SQuAD, DROP, HellaSwag and WMT. It reports that raising β instead cost reward and never recovered DROP or SQuAD ([p. 14](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/Training%20language%20models%20to%20follow%20instructions%20with%20human%20feedback.pdf?page=14&search=Mixing%20in%20pretraining%20updates%20performs%20better)).
- **DPO's account of PPO instability.** DPO argues that PPO's reward is missing a normalisation term, the soft value of $\pi_{ref}$. Without it the policy gradient has high variance, which PPO needs a learned value function or a human-completion baseline to offset. DPO's reparameterised reward needs no baseline ([p. 6, §5.2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/Direct%20Preference%20Optimization.%20Your%20Language%20Model%20is%20Secretly%20a%20Reward%20Model.pdf?dest=subsection.5.2&page=6)). InstructGPT does use both of these remedies: a value network initialised from the reward model (p. 9) and rewards shifted to the labeler demonstrations (p. 8).
- **What DPO's gradient does.** It raises $\log\pi(y_w)$ and lowers $\log\pi(y_l)$. Each pair is weighted by how wrongly the implicit reward currently orders it. Without that weight the model degenerates (p. 4).
- **The empirical claim, with a caveat.** DPO says both methods optimise the same objective and that DPO's reward-vs-KL trade-off on IMDb strictly dominates PPO's ([p. 8, §6.1](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/Direct%20Preference%20Optimization.%20Your%20Language%20Model%20is%20Secretly%20a%20Reward%20Model.pdf?dest=subsection.6.1&page=8)). The library's note on DPO flags that its PPO baselines were off-the-shelf or only lightly tuned. That point comes from the note, not from DPO's text.

**Notation trap:** the papers swap θ and φ. In InstructGPT, $r_\theta$ is the reward model and $\pi_\phi$ the policy. In DPO, $r_\phi$ is the reward model and $\pi_\theta$ the policy.
